ui.chat.remote_compute.card.artifacts_so.role: the tooltip on the disabled logs and results controls
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.artifacts_so.note: It arrives in a later version. Promise no date and no version number.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.binding.role: the line under the run card naming the network it is recorded against
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.binding.tone: two short sentences, plain statement, full stops
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.binding.note: Claim-sensitive: the binding is RECORDED, not enforced, in this version. It is now its own line rather than the last item of the card's fact chain (design round 1, D3). Keep the word for recorded and the negation of enforcement; never promise isolation, segmentation or privacy.

placeholders.network: the network's own name, as the user gave it. Keep it verbatim.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.binding_none.role: the same line when the run carries no network
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.binding_none.tone: two short sentences, plain statement, full stops
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.binding_none.note: States the fact and the absent enforcement, and stops. It must not imply the run was bound by choice or will be bound later.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.cancel.role: the run card's action that stops a live run
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.cancel.note: Stops a run that can still spend. Not a dismiss: the row remains.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.cancel_faile.role: the sentence shown when the cancel request was refused with no sentence of its own
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.cancel_faile.note: Only used when the server's refusal carried no message; the server's own sentence is shown instead whenever it has one.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.charged.role: the amount a settled run was charged
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.charged.tone: past participle plus amount, lower case
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.charged.note: The settled charge the server reports. Never compute or extrapolate it.

placeholders.amount: a locale-formatted USD amount (e.g. $5.09, 5,09 $US, US$5.09). Keep it verbatim.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.forget.role: the run card's action that removes a settled run's record
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.forget.note: Forgets the record of a run that can no longer spend. Softer than delete, and offered only once the run has settled.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.forget_faile.role: the sentence shown when the remove request was refused with no sentence of its own

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.held.role: the amount an unsettled run holds
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.held.tone: past participle plus amount, lower case
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.held.note: A hold is the committed maximum, not a charge.

placeholders.amount: a locale-formatted USD amount (e.g. $5.09, 5,09 $US, US$5.09). Keep it verbatim.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.logs.role: label of the run's logs view
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.logs.note: The run's own output. Disabled in this version with card.artifacts_soon.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.not_found.role: the sentence a gone run's read raises, shown beside its remedy
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.not_found.note: The record is gone, not the run's fault. Name the remedy the button performs (a re-read) rather than apologising.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.results.role: label of the run's results view
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.results.note: The files a run produced. Disabled in this version with card.artifacts_soon.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.status.cance.role: run status: cancelled by a person
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.status.cance.note: Distinct from failed: somebody stopped it.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.status.queue.note: It has been accepted and has not started.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.status.runni.note: Also covers provisioning and starting; keep it true for the whole span.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.status.succe.note: A completed run. It is not a claim that the work inside it succeeded.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.unavailable.role: the run card when its read failed
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.unavailable.note: The card could not be read, so it shows nothing about the run. The remedy is a separate control.

ui.chat.remote_compute.card.untitled.role: the run card's title when the server sent no name
ui.chat.remote_compute.card.untitled.note: A placeholder for a missing name, not a prompt summary.

ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.add_credit.role: the button that opens the billing page after a refusal about payment
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.add_credit.tone: an imperative verb phrase, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.add_credit.note: It opens the account's billing page in the browser; it buys nothing by itself.

ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.push_branc.role: the label naming the act that clears a refusal about an unpushed commit
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.push_branc.tone: an imperative verb phrase, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.push_branc.note: The app does not push; this names what the user has to do in their own tools.

ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.push_branc.role: the explanation shown with that refusal
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.push_branc.note: Never print a shell command: describe the act. The server's own refusal sentence is shown above this one.

ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.refresh.role: the button that re-reads after a refusal saying the row is gone or finished
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.refresh.note: A read, never a retry of the write.

ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.retry.role: the button that repeats a refused request
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.retry.tone: an imperative verb phrase, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.retry.note: Used when the server named no wait.

ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.retry_in.role: the retry action while the server's own wait has not elapsed
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.retry_in.tone: imperative phrase with a countdown, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.retry_in.note: The number is the server's Retry-After, never an estimate. Keep the plural arms and `#`. It is a button label, so keep it short.

placeholders.seconds: whole seconds remaining, from the server's answer

ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.sign_in.role: the button that starts a sign-in after a refusal about the account
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.sign_in.tone: an imperative verb phrase, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.remedy.sign_in.note: Same action as the picker's on-ramp, worded as a button.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.capacity.role: picker row when capacity cannot be provisioned right now
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.capacity.note: Not 'offline' and not a device that went away: this is rented capacity that cannot be provisioned at the moment.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.checking.role: picker row while the capability read is in flight
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.checking.tone: lower-case fragment ending in an ellipsis character
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.checking.note: Says only that a read is happening. Do not guess the outcome.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.create_one.role: the remedy printed after the needs-network row
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.create_one.note: Short: inline after a middot. The how lives in row.sentence.network.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.held.role: money the combined live runs are holding, on the picker row
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.held.tone: verb phrase fragment, lower case, no trailing punctuation
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.held.note: A hold is the committed maximum while unsettled, not a charge: use the word for a temporary hold.

placeholders.amount: a locale-formatted USD amount (e.g. $5.09, 5,09 $US, US$5.09). Keep it verbatim.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.name.role: product name of the rented-capacity option in the chat's device picker
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.name.tone: a proper noun, Latin spelling, never translated
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.name.note: Radient is a company name. Keep it verbatim in every locale.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.needs_network.role: picker row when the device is in no network, so a run cannot be bound
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.needs_network.note: The consequence, not an error. The remedy is printed beside it by row.create_one.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.network_remed.role: the visible remedy line under the Radient row when the device is in no network
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.network_remed.tone: one sentence naming two commands, plain, no exclamation
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.network_remed.note: Visible text rather than only the accessible name (UX round 1, U3): creating a network is CLI-only, so the row prints the commands instead of ending in an imperative with no control behind it. Never translate the command names, the flags or the quoted token placeholder.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.not_offered.role: picker row when the user's switch is on but this deployment runs no remote compute
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.not_offered.note: Distinct from the user's flag and from the account: the deployment does not offer it, so never suggest a remedy the user could perform.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.ready.role: picker row when capacity is ready and no run is live
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.ready.tone: one word, lower case, no punctuation
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.ready.note: Readiness only. Never a price, a rate or a countdown: the app cannot read them.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.retry.role: the action printed after the capacity row, and what selecting the row does
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.retry.note: Short: it sits inline after a middot.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.runs.role: count of live runs on the picker row
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.runs.tone: plural noun fragment, no sentence punctuation
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.runs.note: Use the locale's own plural categories and keep `#` so ICU formats the digits. Only used below the cap; the saturated form is row.runs_capped.

placeholders.count: the number of live runs, 1 to 9

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.runs_capped.tone: fragment with a plus sign, no sentence punctuation
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.runs_capped.note: The count is capped so the money beside it is not: never drop the plus sign, which is what says the number is a floor.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.capa.role: accessible name of the picker row when capacity is unavailable
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.capa.tone: two short sentences: the state, then the affordance
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.capa.note: Selecting the row re-reads. It does not try to buy anything.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.chec.role: accessible name of the picker row while the read is in flight
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.chec.note: Prefixes the product name and restates row.checking with its subject.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.netw.role: accessible name of the picker row when the device is in no network
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.netw.tone: one sentence of fact, then the two commands that fix it
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.netw.note: The backticked runs are terminal commands: keep them exactly as written, in backticks, Latin script and left-to-right even in an RTL locale. Do not translate `lop network init` or `lop network join`.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.not_.role: accessible name of the picker row when the deployment does not offer the family
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.not_.note: Says why the row cannot be used, and offers nothing: no sign-in would help.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.read.role: accessible name of the picker row when ready
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.read.tone: two short sentences: the state, then the affordance
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.read.note: Selecting the row does not start a run: it opens the second level that chooses how the run is bought. Keep that distinction.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.runs.role: accessible name of the picker row while runs are live
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.runs.tone: one sentence, statement then the affordance
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.runs.note: The placeholders carry the visible facts so a screen reader hears the same claim. `factsSuffix` is empty or begins with its own separator: do not add one before it.

placeholders.factsSuffix: empty, or a separator and the remaining facts, e.g. ` · 12m04s · held $15.27`. Keep separators and amount verbatim.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.sign.role: accessible name of the picker row when signed out
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.sign.tone: two short sentences: the reason, then the affordance
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sentence.sign.note: The visible label cannot carry the consequence, so this sentence must: signing in is what makes the row usable, and selecting it starts that sign-in.

ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sign_in.role: picker row when the account is signed out or expired
ui.chat.remote_compute.row.sign_in.note: An on-ramp, not an error: the row is selectable and starts the sign-in. Keep the sense of 'do this to use it', not 'you are not allowed'.

ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.disabled.role: the banner over the runs list when this deployment runs no remote compute
ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.disabled.note: Nothing failed. Keep the same fact as the picker row's not-offered state, phrased for this banner.

ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.empty.role: the runs list when the server holds no runs
ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.empty.note: An answered emptiness, not a failure. The list's own error state is separate.

ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.loading.role: the runs list while its read is in flight
ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.loading.tone: a lower-case fragment ending in an ellipsis character
ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.loading.note: No spinner metaphor and no guess at the outcome.

ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.record_only.role: the banner over the runs list when the account is signed out
ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.record_only.note: These rows are this device's record, not the server's answer, and signing in is what reads the server's rows.

ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.title.role: the heading of the dialog that lists every run

ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.unavailable.role: the banner over the runs list when the server could not report its runs
ui.chat.remote_compute.runs.unavailable.note: The rows shown may be stale. Do not claim they are wrong.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.close.note: Closes the sheet without starting anything.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.directory.l.role: the label above the directory line
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.directory.l.note: The directory the run starts in, shown as a path.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.heading.tone: a short verb phrase with the product name, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.heading.note: It is where a run is configured: the network, how it is bought, the prompt and the directory.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.cha.role: the control that re-opens the network options
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.cha.note: Shown only when there is more than one network to choose from.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.cho.role: the prompt in place of a network name when none is chosen
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.cho.note: A statement of what is missing, not a button label: the options are listed below it.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.cho.role: the reason printed on the tier rows while no network is chosen
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.cho.tone: an imperative fragment, lower case, no punctuation
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.cho.note: Same meaning as network.choose, phrased as a reason on a row rather than a heading.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.lab.role: the label of the network line
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.lab.note: The mesh network the run is recorded against.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.not.role: the same sentence when no network has been chosen yet
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.not.note: The qualification alone: it must state that enforcement is absent without naming a network the user has not chosen. Never say isolated, segmented or private.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.rec.role: the sentence under the network line explaining what the binding does
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.rec.tone: two short sentences, plain statement, full stops
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.network.rec.note: The most claim-sensitive sentence in the surface: the run is RECORDED against the network and access is NOT enforced by it in this version. It is now printed on its own line at body size (design round 1, D3), so the qualification must stand alone as a sentence. Never say isolated, segmented or private.

placeholders.network: the network's own name, as the user gave it. Keep it verbatim.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.prompt.empt.role: the note under the prompt label when the composer is empty
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.prompt.empt.note: The reason, not the remedy; the remedy is typed in the composer.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.prompt.labe.role: the label above the prompt summary
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.prompt.labe.note: The composer's text, shown as one line so the user recognises what will run.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.tone: an imperative verb phrase, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.note: Starting a run spends money and time, so the verb is about starting rather than sending.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.why_.role: the reason the submit is disabled: capacity is unavailable
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.why_.note: Same fact as row.capacity, at the commit control.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.why_.role: the reason the submit is disabled: the conversation has no directory
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.why_.note: The pane's own directory has not been resolved yet; nothing is wrong with the server.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.why_.role: the reason the submit is disabled: no network chosen
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.why_.note: Names the decision the user has not made yet.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.why_.role: the reason the submit is disabled: the composer is empty
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submit.why_.note: A run needs a prompt, and the prompt is the composer's text.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submitting.role: the submit button while the run is being created
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submitting.tone: a present-participle fragment ending in an ellipsis character
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.submitting.note: Spends nothing new on its own; the press already did.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.capaci.role: why the on-demand tier cannot be chosen right now
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.capaci.note: The same fact as row.capacity, on a row. No remedy text here.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.cloud_.role: one shape fact about the on-demand tier, under its title
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.cloud_.tone: a fragment, lower case, middot separators
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.cloud_.note: No price and no duration: the app cannot read rates and has no measured timings. Describe the shape only - one run, one answer, then gone. Keep the middots.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.cloud_.role: the line under the tier list naming the tier a run will use
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.cloud_.note: Replaces a check mark and a selected ground that asserted a choice nobody made while only one tier can be bought (design round 1, D10). It names the tier exactly as the tier row does.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.cloud_.role: the name of the on-demand tier
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.cloud_.tone: two words or fewer, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.cloud_.note: The product's name for the tier chosen per run: translate the concept and keep it recognisable, not as a literal cloud plus the verb run.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.role: one shape fact about the long-lived tier
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.tone: a fragment, lower case, middot separators
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.note: Shape only: it keeps a workspace and its files. No price, no duration, no comparison with the other tier.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.role: one shape fact about the interruptible option
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.tone: a fragment, lower case, middot separators
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.note: Names the trade: interruptible, cheaper, can be reclaimed. No price and no notice period.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.role: the name of the interruptible option under the long-lived tier
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.note: Radient's word for interruptible capacity: translate the concept (interruptible, reclaimable), not as a literal stain.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.role: the name of the long-lived tier
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.note: The API's own word is a dedicated workload. Keep the sense of a reserved, long-lived workspace.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.role: why the long-lived tier and its spot option cannot be chosen yet
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.tone: two words, lower case, no punctuation
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.dedica.note: Not available yet; promise no date, no version number.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.group_.role: the small heading over the tier rows
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.group_.tone: a short noun phrase, sentence case, no punctuation
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.tier.group_.note: Introduces the rows describing what kind of run the tiers are (one-shot vs long-lived workspace) - not how it is paid for, because the sheet quotes no price (design round 1, D6). It is not a sentence and needs no verb agreement with the row count.

ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.view_runs.role: the link to the runs list in the sheet's footer
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.view_runs.tone: an imperative verb phrase, sentence case
ui.chat.remote_compute.sheet.view_runs.note: Opens a list of every run the server holds, including ones this conversation did not start.

ui.chat.remote_compute.store.accepted_wi.role: error sentence when the server accepted a start but returned no run row
ui.chat.remote_compute.store.accepted_wi.note: The run may exist upstream, so this must not say nothing was started; it says the row is missing. The idempotency key makes the retry safe.

ui.chat.remote_compute.store.refused.role: error sentence when the server refused a request without a code this app knows
ui.chat.remote_compute.store.refused.note: The refusal came from the server and carried no message. Never add a remedy here: an invented on-ramp for an unknown code is how a user gets sent to a sign-in for a 404.

ui.chat.remote_compute.store.transport.role: error sentence when the request never reached the local server
ui.chat.remote_compute.store.transport.tone: two short sentences, plain, no blame
ui.chat.remote_compute.store.transport.note: The daemon was unreachable, so nothing is known about the outcome. It must not claim the run failed or that nothing was charged.
